claims.claim: Procopius of Gaza was a Christian sophist and rhetorician, one of the most important representatives of the Rhetorical School of Gaza, born roughly in 465–470 and died approximately 526–530.
Procopius succeeded Aeneas as the head of the school of Gaza.
A collection of 163 elaborately rhetorical letters by Procopius has survived, though other sources mention 165 or 174 letters.
The letters are devoid of theological interest but supply biographical data.
Letter 2 of Procopius was written to Hieronymus, a correspondent of Procopius, from Gaza in Palaestina Prima to Elusa in Palaestina Tertia, dated approximately c. 515 AD.
The letter makes a learned miniature essay out of homesickness, Egyptian abundance, Odysseus, Sparta, and the Nile.
The only sources for Procopius' life are his surviving letters and the funeral oration composed and delivered by his pupil, Choricius.
Procopius was the preceptor of Choricius the sophist.

The letters provide insights into sophistic self-fashioning, the textual tradition, and editorial challenges, and contextualize Procopius's work within the broader landscape of rhetorical and monastic activity of 6th-century Palestine.
